evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: name (Rob Fields), moving day (October 1st), city-to-city route (8807 Bra Crest Drive, San Antonio to 14925 Moss Glen, San Antonio), approximate size (2800 sq ft primary, 1300 sq ft destination)
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked late, after extensive probing: 'Okay, are we downsizing?' followed by logistics review. No explicit 'what are your biggest concerns' framing.
evidence_quotes.walkthrough_branch: Rep correctly identified 2800 sq ft home qualifies for virtual walkthrough and offered it: 'normally based on your home size, we do a virtual walkthrough... Do you have time to complete the virtual walk through today?'
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (2-story, 1-story), bedrooms (2, 2), rooms (kitchen noted), walking distance (20 feet), access concerns (flat, driveway parking confirmed), special items (washer/dryer, fridge), box count (25 boxes), downsizing status confirmed
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: 'the total number of boxes that we're moving would be $45' (miscommunication, then clarified to 25 boxes)

top_strength: Rep thoroughly gathered all logistics details and correctly identified and offered the virtual walkthrough for a 2,800 sq ft home, then properly pivoted to a photo/video submission process when customer couldn't do real-time walkthrough.
coaching_note: Section 1 is missing the quid pro quo framing entirely — rep jumped straight into problem-solving (rain question) and logistics probing without time-boxing the call or getting explicit buy-in before asking discovery questions.
